Definition: to station, in various applications (literally or figuratively)
BiblicalUsage: 1) to stand, take one's stand, stand upright, be set (over), establish; 1a) (Niphal); 1a1) to station oneself, take one's stand; 1a2) to stand, be stationed; 1a3) to stand, take an upright position; 1a4) to be stationed, be appointed; 1a5) deputy, prefect, appointed, deputed (subst); 1a6) to stand firm; 1b) (Hiphil); 1b1) to station, set; 1b2) to set up, erect; 1b3) to cause to stand erect; 1b4) to fix, establish; 1c) (Hophal) to be fixed, be determined, be stationary
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
